limitations: Automated Tier 3 implementation qualification only; no human Tier 1 review or Tier 2 usage certification.
The source describes a generic benchmark topology, not an identified historical winning solution. No competitive accuracy or true strength-of-schedule claim is made.
Complete synthetic graph results match the unchanged reference. Matrix-only tests demonstrate mechanical reuse, not empirical cross-domain accuracy.

Season feature aggregation and mirrored chronological pairing retain the source recipe. Dense standardized binary fitting supports arbitrary positive feature widths; sigmoid fit/predict and ordered sum remain independently bound generic providers.
Intermediate provenance and population independence are caller responsibilities; shape and chronology checks do not authenticate them.
Existing sigmoid fitting does not check optimizer success. Finite calibration coefficients do not establish convergence; base logistic fitting does treat ConvergenceWarning as an error.
Installed package files match their own RECORD hashes; publisher authenticity, clean deployment, optional extras and other platforms remain unqualified.
Provider publication transaction gates and stored corrected-original CDG execution/publication remain separate requirements.
The original intake has only a generic benchmark description and Kaggle homepage citation; no historical winner or source-code parity is claimed.
The explicitly permitted logistic branch is fully implemented. XGBoost is an alternative branch, not an omitted mandatory stage.
PageRank remains a declared graph feature; the intake claim of true strength of schedule is unsupported and explicitly corrected.

Prediction rows are caller-enumerated. To evaluate every possible matchup, callers must provide all desired ordered pairs; the stored execution exercises all six pairs among three synthetic teams. The implementation does not infer tournament membership or silently add rows.

Current NumPy is 2.2.6 rather than historical 2.4.2. Current active requirements, actual imports, installed files and fresh full-reference comparisons pass; historical environment equivalence is not claimed.
Preparation validates only root fields, finite JSON and nonempty populations. Downstream stages enforce detailed numerical and chronological contracts.
Original history and derivative are preserved. Native publication, atomic activation and served selection remain separate gates.
qualification.parameter_contract: Require a dictionary with exactly version, games, training, calibration, prediction, feature_controls, regularization, max_iterations, tolerance and seed. Require json.dumps with allow_nan=False to succeed. Version is Python integer one excluding bool. Feature controls must be a dictionary with exactly free_throw_weight, elo_initial, elo_k, elo_scale, pagerank_alpha, pagerank_tolerance and pagerank_iterations. Games, training, calibration and prediction must each be a nonempty Python list. Return frozen Prepared wrapping a deep-copied payload; the nested dictionary remains mutable. This boundary does not validate individual game or target fields, numeric control ranges, team features, temporal independence, class balance or optimizer convergence. These checks occur in downstream feature, pairing and fitting stages. No model fitting, calibration, external data parsing or accuracy certification occurs here. No serialized byte-size bound or authenticated provenance is implemented. Downstream contracts: Require explicit finite feature and optimizer controls. Preserve the original possessions formula and ratios of summed totals, per-season rating resets, stable custom-scale Elo expectation, directed weighted PageRank with explicit tolerance and iteration budget, sorted game order, unique game chronology and rejection of tied completed games. PageRank exhaustion propagates as an error. Team vectors are float64 with five components: offensive efficiency, defensive efficiency, turnover rate, PageRank and Elo. No training or calibration occurs. Deep-copy and validate exact packet fields. Require nonnegative Python integer season/team/order identifiers, distinct teams known to their season, exact target row fields and binary fitting/calibration outcomes. Every target follows its season feature cutoff. Labeled (season,order) identities are unique. All training seasons precede all calibration seasons, which precede all prediction seasons. Require at least two original fitting and two calibration matchups. Concatenate A, B and A-B for each orientation; append reversed rows and complemented labels in source order. Reject invalid optimizer controls. Supplied features and chronology must be trustworthy; structural checks do not authenticate provenance. Prevalidate every input before fitting. Matrices are nonempty finite float64 rank-two arrays with a shared arbitrary positive feature width; forward and reverse shapes match. Labels are aligned int64 rank-one arrays with both 0 and 1 represented and at least two rows per labeled population. Copy arrays before use. Seed is a Python integer in [0,2**32); iteration budget is a positive Python integer; C and tolerance are finite positive Python int/float excluding bool. Fit StandardScaler then LogisticRegression using lbfgs and explicit controls. Promote ConvergenceWarning to an error. Require classes [0,1]. Evaluate three separate decision_function calls for calibration, forward and reverse; require finite rank-one float64 scores. No base refit during external calibration. Caller establishes independent populations and shared feature meaning; this stage does not prove either. Prediction rows are caller-enumerated; supply all desired ordered pairs to cover all matchups. No automatic tournament membership or pair enumeration. Game dictionaries contain exactly season, order, a, b, a_box and b_box. Each box contains exactly points, field_goal_attempts, free_throw_attempts, offensive_rebounds and turnovers, all nonnegative Python integers excluding bool; estimated possessions must be positive and completed scores unequal. Target rows contain season, order, a and b, plus outcome for training/calibration. Season, order and team slots are nonnegative Python integers excluding bool; teams are distinct. Outcome is integer zero or one. Feature controls are finite: free_throw_weight in [0,1], elo_k and elo_scale positive, pagerank_alpha in (0,1), pagerank_tolerance positive and pagerank_iterations a positive Python integer. Elo initialization is finite. Regularization is positive C, tolerance positive, max_iterations a positive Python integer, and seed a Python integer in [0,2**32).
qualification.output_contract: Strict JSON probabilities plus training_rows, calibration_rows and predicted_matchups. Probabilities are in caller prediction order, computed as .5*(forward+1-reverse) with left-ordered arithmetic. Counts for training and calibration include mirrored rows. Every invocation fits a fresh base model and held-out sigmoid state. No fitted model object is returned.
